newsitem.title: USA: Consumers sees 67 MW Mich. nuke up Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Consumers sees 67 MW Mich. nuke up Tuesday.

text.p: Consumers Power Co expects its 67 megawatt (MW) Big Rock Point 1 nuclear station to return to service Tuesday, the company said Monday.
"If things go well...we could be back on line tomorrow," said on-site plant spokesman Tim Petrosky.
A failure of the pressure control mechanism to the unit's admission valves resulted in an automatic shutdown today.
The admission valves regulate the pressure of the steam entering the plant's turbine.
Big Rock Point 1 in Charlevoix, Mich., accounts for one percent of the utility's installed generation capacity.
The smaller of the two nuclear plants operated by Consumers Power, it was shut Sept 10 for roughly six days to repair a valve leak.
Consumers' other nuclear plant, the 780 MW Palisades 1 in South Haven, Mich., is operating at full output.
Consumers Power is a subsidary of CMS Energy Corp.
